question: After three additions from erasure at eight, does the anonymous three-distinction relation determine what the four can do together after one more addition?

public_inputs.population: All reachable triples of additions from each of the thirteen published cut inputs. Count cut-indexed terminal column sets as in FRESH-THREE and verify their probabilities. A context comprises the full eleven-distinction table and the evaluator's three-element set.
public_inputs.rule: Use the same signed fewest-states conservative growth, with up to three allowed ternary knots, an untied fresh distinction, uniform over literal minimizing extensions and both orientations counted. The grower receives no cohort marks.
public_inputs.four_observation: Allowed four-bit assignments, with row multiplicities discarded. Quotient by independent value swaps and permutations of the three earlier additions, marking the latest only for evaluation. Also compute the quotient permitting all four coordinates to permute.

forbidden_inputs: Letting the growth rule consult column ages, source labels, history, evaluator group or coins from earlier choices
Comparing type-conditioned averages in place of full context-by-context sufficiency
Counting a change of labelling or the inherited ternary relation alone as a new predictive effect
Using outcome classes once each instead of summing the probabilities of different legal moves and paths
primary_observable: Within each ternary type (six-state knot or free eight-state triple), count distinct conditional four-state probability laws and distinct sets of attainable four-state relation classes across the full contexts under both observation conventions.
decision_rule: Exact sufficiency for probabilities requires a single conditional law in the group. Possibility sufficiency requires a single set of outcomes. Exhibit a reachable witness pair for any failure. A possibility present in one context and absent in another is a stronger witness than unequal positive probabilities.
secondary_observables: k is the number of the three pairs of earlier additions which, together with the fourth, form a six-state knot. Report the range and probability of k>=1 within each ternary type, pooling with true growth weights and equal priors over the two six-distinction starts.

The fourth is determined by the three if the four-column projection has the same number of rows as the three-column projection. Record ranges and pooled probabilities; inspect the six-state triple's unique unused-or-occupied determined column.
Prefer witnesses from distinct eight-cut isomorphism classes with identical added columns up to signs. Reproduce their reachability and conditional fourth extensions with the separate literal rule.
cheapest_meaningful_control: Both six- and eight-state triples occur with known probabilities at eleven. A recoded context must preserve the fourth law. Projection back to three must recover its initial type. Distinguish possibilities involving the fourth from inheritance of the preceding triple.
resource_ceiling: Thirteen initial eight-cut classes and 22,475 indexed eleven-distinction contexts; one further addition per context, no sampling and no larger sizes. Every zero-cost shortcut must verify an available fill at every reached parent or use the original minimization.
first_executable_signal: Validate canonicalization on synthetic four-column tables and recover the preceding experiment's per-cut triple sizes and probabilities.
stop_rule: Stop after the two sufficiency tests, the free-triple comparison and frozen checks through twelve total distinctions.
nonclaims: The complete measurement belongs to these starts and the supplied growth rule.
Context-dependent probabilities at a fixed type disprove exact sufficiency for that type; an average can still predict a particular later feature.
